assigned.title: notFound() never reaches the wire: dead addresses answer 200
assigned.notes: IMPLEMENTED IN THE TREE AND NEVER CLAIMED, like the rest of recovery packet 1 -- but PARTIALLY, and the two gaps are different in kind. This is the fifth task found in that state, and its code landed while it sat BACKLOG and unowned: control/events.jsonl records apps/web/src/app/loading.tsx and page.tsx being edited as belonging to PL-0704 while it was blocked on a lifecycle dependency. So it must be started with --reconcile-existing, never against HEAD. IT IS A MODIFICATION TASK IN THE REVIEWER'S TAXONOMY, MOSTLY, and that changes the probe. Its central act was a DELETION -- the root loading.tsx removed -- and marker absence cannot witness a deletion. What it also did, and what CAN be witnessed, is introduce two named components where anonymous route-level skeletons used to be: CatalogSkeleton in app/page.tsx and PlaybackLoading in app/watch/[contentId]/page.tsx, each now a Suspense fallback sitting BELOW the existence decision rather than a loading file wrapping the whole segment. Those two names are new even though their markup is not, so a pickaxe on the names finds the relocation, which is precisely this task's work. Use them as the witnesses; do not use the deleted file. TWO GAPS AGAINST THE ACCEPTANCE, AND ONLY ONE IS A CODE GAP. FIRST, THE TITLE SKELETON, WHICH I BELIEVE IS A CONTRACT GAP RATHER THAN A DEFECT AND AM FLAGGING FOR A RULING RATHER THAN FIXING. The acceptance says any fix must KEEP the loading skeletons rather than deleting them to move a status code. Home and watch comply: both relocated their skeleton into a Suspense boundary below a cheap existence check that consults nobody. The title route did not -- it deleted its skeleton outright -- and its own header argues why: on that route a status line precedes the first body byte, so no byte may be sent before the catalog answers whether the title exists, which is the definition of having nothing to stream. A full-page skeleton there IS the defect the task exists to remove. The only honest way to restore one would be a section whose data does not depend on the title existing, and none exists today. So the code looks right and the clause looks over-general. I am not rewriting the acceptance to match the code unasked -- that is the move the reviewer has twice had to authorise explicitly, on PL-0205's wording and on PL-0706's -- so it is proposed here and left for the verdict. SECOND, THE PRODUCTION-MODE 404, WHICH IS NOT THIS TASK'S TO CLOSE. An unknown title answers 404 under development and 200 with a refusal panel under production, and that is correct rather than broken: on a hosted build no catalog metadata source is constructible, so loadTitleDetail reports error rather than not-found, notFound() is unreachable, and a build that answered 404 there would be claiming an absence it never looked for. The precondition is a catalog source that exists in a deployment, which is PL-0305's, now READY since PL-0105 completed. ALLOWEDPATHS CORRECTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. apps/web/src/app/(home)/** is DROPPED: it is a dead declaration for a route-group approach that was considered and rejected, it reserves a directory that does not exist, and it starves nothing only by accident. apps/web/src/app/loading.tsx is KEPT even though the file is deleted, because the deletion is the change and a surface that omitted it would not fingerprint the task's central act. TWO PATHS ADDED. docs/E2E.md, because it and .github/workflows/ci.yml currently CONTRADICT EACH OTHER about whether the two 404 assertions have ever been observed passing -- E2E.md claims an executed 2026-09-05 pass on all four browser projects, ci.yml says UNKNOWN, expected to pass, never observed passing -- and settling that is exactly what this task's EXECUTED clause is about. It is declared by PL-0706, which is DONE, and by PL-0703, which is BLOCKED, so no active conflict. And .github/workflows/ci.yml, which UNTIL NOW WAS DECLARED BY NO TASK IN THE REPOSITORY AT ALL: every CI change this project has made has landed outside every declared surface. That is a real declaration hole rather than a convenience, and this task adopting it is a partial fix at best -- the file is repository governance rather than frontend, and it should eventually belong to whatever task adopts CLAUDE.md and control/README.md, which are undeclared for the same reason.
assigned.acceptance: An unknown title id and a malformed watch id each answer HTTP 404 rather than a skeleton served at 200, proven by an EXECUTED Playwright run ON THE PINNED BROWSER REVISION rather than by a route calling notFound(), and rather than by a run on a substituted revision. The cause is that a segment's loading file wraps that segment in Suspense, so React flushes the shell at 200 before the access-fallback error escapes the render and Next can set the status; the root loading file wraps every route in the application, so per-route fixes alone are insufficient. THE SKELETON CLAUSE, AMENDED. Any fix must RELOCATE the loading skeletons below the existence decision rather than deleting them to move a status code, ON EVERY ROUTE WHERE A SECTION'S DATA DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE ADDRESS EXISTING. The title route is exempt, and the exemption is reasoned rather than granted: a well-formed unknown title id is indistinguishable from a real one until the catalog answers, the status line precedes the first body byte, so no byte may be sent before that load resolves -- which is the definition of having nothing to stream. A full-page skeleton there IS the defect this task exists to remove, so the unamended clause required the defect on one of the three routes it governs. The exemption is EMPIRICAL AND REVERSIBLE, not permanent: the moment the title page grows a section whose data does not depend on the title existing -- recommendations, continue-watching, anything PL-0301 or PL-0501 fetches separately -- it gains an in-page Suspense below the decision exactly as the watch route has, and this clause binds again. Home and watch satisfy it today and a positive check proves each, because the original wording was satisfied by a repository with no skeletons in it at all: every assertion was a not.toContain on a string that exists nowhere. DEPENDS ON PL-0103 because the title route is that task's declared write surface; this is a lifecycle dependency, not a technical one.

typecheck.evidence: npx turbo run typecheck --force at integrated head e097590ee79e112f26073b293a4ad7fbb2bd1fd6, exit 0, 9 of 9 tasks and 0 cached. npm run typecheck in e2e/ also exit 0.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force at integrated head e097590ee79e112f26073b293a4ad7fbb2bd1fd6, exit 0, 15 of 15 tasks and 0 cached, 2112 passed 1 skipped 0 failed. This round adds one case to apps/web/src/app/watch/route-loading-boundaries.test.ts, 'holds the title route to its exemption, and to the clause the moment it lapses': the title page may declare no Suspense, which is today's tree, OR one whose fallback is a NAMED skeleton component defined in the page, which is the state the amended clause requires once the exemption lapses. It is written without an early return so it always evaluates, it asserts the premise -- that the route still decides existence -- before the exemption, and it was confirmed non-vacuous in both directions: an anonymous fallback fails it with the message a contributor needs, and the same boundary with a defined skeleton passes. THE BLIND SPOT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN CLAIMED AWAY: the clause's trigger is semantic, so a contributor who adds an independent title-page section and streams nothing for it leaves both gates green. The reversal is caught where it becomes VISIBLE, not where it becomes TRUE, and that is stated in the test, in the page header and in docs/E2E.md.

e2e.evidence: EXECUTED ON THE PINNED BROWSER REVISION. This SUPERSEDES the round-42 evidence, which ran on Chromium revision 1194 behind a symlink shim presenting it as 1234; the commander ruled that acceptable as narrow local evidence and NOT as pinned-browser verification, and the constraint that forced it is gone -- cdn.playwright.dev is reachable from this container and npx playwright install chromium placed revision 1234 in the default cache. @playwright/test 1.62.1 requires 1234 and the binary answers 'Google Chrome for Testing 151.0.7922.34'; the 1194 build in /opt/pw-browsers answers 'Chromium 141.0.7390.37', four milestones apart. HOW THE REVISION WAS PROVEN RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because 'it ran' is exactly what the shim round could also have said: playwright install --dry-run under the same environment prints the install location as /root/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1234, while under the ambient environment it prints /opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1234, a path that does not exist -- so a run with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH left in place would have FAILED to find an executable rather than quietly using 1194; DEBUG=pw:browser logged exactly one launch path, the 1234 headless shell; and the two binaries were asked their versions directly. Every invocation used env -u PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH -u PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD; e2e/playwright.config.ts was NOT edited, no executablePath and no channel were set, and nothing in e2e/ changed to make the run work. THE RUNS, at integrated head e097590ee79e112f26073b293a4ad7fbb2bd1fd6, from e2e/ after npm ci there: development, LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development npx playwright test --project=api --project=chromium, exit 0, 43 passed 3 skipped 0 failed; production, the default, same projects, exit 0, 34 passed 12 skipped 0 failed. Asserted statuses unchanged from the shim run: /title/no-such-title-pl0701 is 404 under development and 200 with catalog_source_not_configured under production; /watch/Not%20A%20Valid%20Id is 404 in BOTH modes; / and /watch/<demo id> are 200 WITH their skeleton strings present; and /title/<demo id> is 200 with NO 'Loading title', which is the positive form of the exemption's premise and is new this round, because a not.toContain on an unknown id cannot distinguish 'refused before any byte' from 'this string is nowhere in the repository'. Second witness: the dev server's own log recorded GET /title/no-such-title-pl0701 404 and GET /watch/Not%20A%20Valid%20Id 404. BEHAVIOURAL DIFFERENCE FROM 1194: NONE -- same counts, same skips, same statuses, no new flake -- and that is reported as a finding rather than as reassurance, because a newer Chromium could legitimately have changed Suspense flush behaviour, which is why the revision is pinned at all. WHAT THIS IS STILL NOT: it is two projects, not the device matrix -- WebKit, mobile-safari and Firefox were not launched, so PL-0705's WebKit clause is untouched -- it is one run per mode with retries 0, and it is NOT the CI job. No claim is made that the CI job will be green: a container run is a different machine, a different install path, a warm turbo cache and CI unset, so reuseExistingServer was on and forbidOnly off. The CI workflow as configured would install the pinned revision from the lockfile-pinned @playwright/test with no version literal, and run the same two projects -- but no run of it has ever been observed.

implementationBaseProvenance.reason: The base is f6c4b942ebbd02fd3fa9ed8f74fde4fc603affc2, the first parent of 719d2d7c31465901f3dbee1e936a180e87c3d44f, derived from history rather than named: 719d2d7 is the one commit that deletes all three loading files, retires HomeLoading and WatchLoading, and introduces CatalogSkeleton and PlaybackLoading, and 'git grep <Suspense> f6c4b94 -- apps/web/src/app' returns only a prose comment, so not one Suspense boundary of this task's arrangement existed in the base tree under any name or in any file. Because the two named witnesses are relocations and could have carried the PL-0205 risk, they are backed by that structural absence, by the paired disappearance of HomeLoading and WatchLoading in the same commit, and by route-loading-boundaries.test.ts being a genuine add there -- the only renames in this repository are PL-AI-0006's four packages/contracts moves, outside this surface. The whole declared surface was swept rename-aware with --full-history plus --follow on the five leaf paths and a conservative 13-file enumeration of title/** and watch/**, reconstructing the deleted apps/web/src/app/loading.tsx deliberately; that yields exactly 23 pre-base commits, every one pre-existing work: c9efc49, 5399c92 and 4091a2b build the three loading files that are the defect, ba2bf47 writes the two 404 assertions as PL-0701's acceptance harness twelve days before this task existed, 8b1172b is the first executed run, which created PL-0704 in control/tasks.json and states in the code that the fix is not done here, and c469e92 adds the comment DO NOT DELETE THIS TO RECOVER THE 404 ... The status is PL-0704's to fix, in the root file. The two document paths were proven separately because that is what sank PL-0601 and PL-0401: .github/workflows/ci.yml contains no 404, loading, skeleton or PL-0704 text whatsoever at the base and gains the entire 404 CI record at 719d2d7, while docs/E2E.md carries only 8b1172b's failing-run report whose prescribed route-group remedy this task rejected rather than implemented. The probes were proven before use, reproducing gpt-architect's own PL-0603 re-derivation exactly and reproducing the three-deletions-one-survivor loading-file set recorded in control/events.jsonl. ONE CLASSIFICATION IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS FLAGGED RATHER THAN BURIED: ba2bf47 and 8b1172b put this task's exact subject matter on its declared e2e and docs paths before the base. They are classified as the task's input rather than its implementation, because ba2bf47 predates PL-0704's existence in control/tasks.json by twelve days and was written by PL-0701's harness lane as an expected-to-pass assertion, and 8b1172b is the commit that created PL-0704, says in the code being changed that the fix is not done here, and proposes a route-group remedy PL-0704 recorded as considered and rejected. If the reviewer rules that authoring a deliberately-red acceptance assertion is part of delivering that acceptance, this base moves and this derivation is wrong.

assigned.acceptanceAmendment: AMENDED 2026-09-15, round 43, by commander instruction, and recorded as an amendment rather than applied silently. Two changes. FIRST, the title-route exemption, which the round-42 implementation flagged for a ruling rather than fixing: the implementer's view was 'amend the clause, do not amend the code', the commander ruled the same way, and the reasoning is now in the acceptance itself so a later reader cannot mistake the exemption for an oversight. The previous wording is preserved verbatim in acceptancePriorToAmendment, because an acceptance criterion that quietly changes shape is indistinguishable from one that was never met. SECOND, the e2e clause now says PINNED BROWSER REVISION explicitly. Round 42 recorded an executed run on Chromium revision 1194 behind a symlink shim presenting it as 1234, disclosed in the gate evidence and in docs/E2E.md, because playwright install was unavailable in that environment. The commander ruled that acceptable as narrow local evidence and NOT as pinned-browser verification. The constraint has since been removed -- cdn.playwright.dev is reachable from this container and revision 1234, Chrome Headless Shell 151.0.7922.34, is installed -- so the clause now demands what is actually achievable rather than what was achievable last round, and the substituted-revision run must be superseded rather than defended.
